chief_complaint: chronic diarrhea, severe weight loss, and oral thrush
hpi_details: 35M presents with a 2-month history of non-bloody watery diarrhea, extreme fatigue, and a 20-pound weight loss. He also complains that his mouth hurts and he has thick white patches on his tongue and inner cheeks.
ideas: thinks he has a bad stomach bug
concerns: terrified about his rapid weight loss
expectations: wants a cure for his diarrhea
social_hx: History of IV drug use, multiple sexual partners

core_concepts: Oral candidiasis (thrush) in a young, otherwise healthy adult without recent antibiotics is a major red flag for severe immunosuppression (HIV).
Chronic diarrhea and wasting are AIDS-defining conditions.
common_misconceptions: Treating the thrush without investigating the underlying cause of immunosuppression.
dangerous_errors: Failing to offer HIV testing in patients presenting with opportunistic infections.
management_principles: HIV screening (4th gen Ag/Ab test), CD4 count, viral load, treat opportunistic infections, initiate ART when appropriate.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 35M with chronic diarrhea, significant weight loss, and painful white oral plaques.
reference_soap.objective: Cachectic. Oropharynx shows thick white removable plaques on erythematous bases (Candidiasis).
reference_soap.assessment: Suspected advanced HIV infection (AIDS) with oral candidiasis and HIV enteropathy/wasting.
reference_soap.plan: Offer and perform HIV 1/2 Ag/Ab screening. Start oral Fluconazole for thrush. Order stool studies for opportunistic pathogens (Cryptosporidium, MAC). Infectious disease consult.

learning_objectives: Recognize oral thrush in an adult as a potential indicator of HIV infection.

teaching.one_liner: Young adult with severe weight loss, chronic diarrhea, and oral candidiasis highly suspicious for advanced HIV.

must_ask.say: How long have you had the diarrhea, and is there any blood in it?
How much weight have you lost, and over what period of time?
Have you noticed white patches in your mouth, or pain when swallowing?
Have you ever been tested for HIV, and do you have any risk factors like unprotected sex or IV drug use?
Have you had a cough, shortness of breath, or vision changes?

history.answer: I've had severe diarrhea that just won't stop for the past two months, and I've lost a shocking amount of weight.
It started around two months ago and has been going on continuously every single day without any breaks.
I go about five or six times a day, and it's large amounts of pure watery stool without any oiliness or foul smell.
No, I have never seen any blood or mucus in the toilet or on the toilet paper.
Yes, it wakes me up from my sleep two or three times every night with an urgent need to run to the bathroom.
I get mild cramping all over my stomach right before I have to go, but it eases up afterward and I don't feel like I still have to push when I'm done.
I have had low fevers off and on, and I've been waking up drenched in night sweats several nights a week for the past month.
My mouth is very dry, I feel lightheaded whenever I stand up fast, and I'm peeing much less than usual and it's very dark.
I haven't eaten any raw meat, seafood, or buffet food, and nobody I know or live near has had any stomach issues.
No, I haven't traveled out of town, gone hiking or camping, or drunk any unfiltered or stream water.
No, I haven't taken any antibiotics, started any new medications, or been admitted to the hospital recently.
I've lost about 20 pounds over these past two months without trying at all, and all my clothes are falling off me.
No, avoiding milk or bread doesn't change anything; everything I eat or drink turns right into watery diarrhea.
I am stressed because of how sick I feel, but this isn't from stress, and I never get constipated.
My joints don't ache, my eyes aren't red, and I haven't noticed new skin rashes, but my mouth is terribly painful.
No, my heart doesn't race, I don't feel sensitive to heat during the day, and my face doesn't flush red.
It hurts a lot to eat or swallow, and I have these thick white creamy patches all over my tongue and inside both cheeks.
I've been feeling completely drained and exhausted all day long, but I haven't had a persistent cough, trouble breathing, or vision problems.
I used to inject drugs intravenously and shared needles with others in the past, though I haven't done that recently.
I've had multiple sexual partners over the past few years, and we haven't always used condoms.
I thought maybe I caught a really bad stomach bug or a parasite that my body simply can't clear on its own.
I am terrified by how fast I'm losing weight and how weak I am getting; I feel like my body is wasting away.
I really hope you can find out what is causing this, stop the diarrhea, and help me regain my strength.
I don't have any history of chronic medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or inflammatory bowel disease.
I have never had any surgeries and I've never been admitted to a hospital before.
I'm not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, or herbal supplements right now.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I smoke about half a pack of cigarettes a day and have smoked for the past ten years.
I only have two or three beers on the weekend once in a while.
I work as a retail clerk at a local shop and live alone in an apartment.
There is no history of chronic gastrointestinal disorders, colon cancer, or thyroid disease in my family.

exam.finding: Patient appears chronically ill, fatigued, and visibly cachectic with temporal wasting.
Blood pressure 108/70 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 37.3°C, SpO2 98% on ambient air.
Mild conjunctival pallor noted bilaterally; sclerae are non-icteric.
Dry oral mucosa with thick, white, curd-like plaques covering the tongue and buccal surfaces that scrape off leaving raw, erythematous bases.
Multiple discrete, nontender, rubbery, mobile lymph nodes palpable in the anterior and posterior cervical chains bilaterally.
Normal thyroid size and consistency, smooth without palpable nodules or tenderness.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally throughout all lung fields without wheezing, rales, or rhonchi.
Regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard.
Scaphoid and wasted abdominal contour with prominent bony landmarks; no surgical scars, caput medusae, or distension.
Hyperactive, rushing bowel sounds auscultated in all four quadrants; no vascular bruits.
Abdomen is soft and scaphoid with mild diffuse non-localized tenderness to deep palpation, without guarding or rigidity.
No rebound tenderness elicited in any quadrant.
Normal anal sphincter tone, empty rectal vault without masses or hemorrhoids, and loose watery stool on glove that tests negative for occult blood.
Decreased skin turgor with delayed skin recoil, dry skin, and visible venous track marks in the bilateral antecubital fossae without active cellulitis.
No pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities; capillary refill time is mildly delayed at approximately two seconds.
